From: marcus_lin@redwood.com

Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-28T08:12:50Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: [ALERT] Spike in 502/503s + 429s across APAC + EU — checkout impact

Quick summary from infra: we see concurrent symptoms in the APAC and EU edge load balancers — elevated upstream 502/503 and client 429s. Initial indicators:
- Sudden increase in small, bursty requests from a subset of client IPs leading to queue saturation on our shared edge proxies.
- KV-cache miss rate rose ~5x which increased origin load.
- A recent kernel parameter tweak (tcp_tw_reuse) rolled across a canary group earlier this morning — rolling back to confirm.

Immediate mitigations applied (08:09 UTC):
- Scoped rate-limit relaxation for Atlas customer on eu and apac route (temporary).
- Forced cache warm for top-10 Atlas prefixes.
- Rolling rollback of kernel tweak to the previous configuration in the canary pool.

Monitoring: error rate dropping in apac edge (08:18) but EU still noisy. Continuing investigation into whether our LB connection churn + origin overload produced cascading 502s and client retry storms (many clients reattempting quickly -> 429s). ETA for stable baseline ~30-45m if rollback holds.

Marcus Lin
SRE — Serving Runtime

Evelyn/Marcus — thanks for the quick response. We did not deploy anything on our side during that window; our side is stable. We see our retry client library doing aggressive retries (0.5s backoff) which is amplifying the load. We can adjust but need Redwood to stabilize the edge so retries stop failing.

Two urgent asks:
- Can Redwood pause global auto-retries (or apply a per-customer backoff) for Atlas?
- Can you share an ETA and whether a credit/RA will be considered — this is a material outage for our weekend sale.

Sara

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-28T09:02:10Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: [ALERT] Spike in 502/503s + 429s across APAC + EU — checkout impact

Update: EU edge shows significant improvement after isolating the problematic proxy pool and diverting Atlas traffic to a cold-path cluster. We've enabled per-customer backoff rules and increased our ingress connection limit for Dedicated routes for the affected clusters. Metrics: 502 rate from 27% -> 6% in EU; APAC down to 12% and trending downward.

Action items for next 2 hours:
- Full postmortem draft (include root cause, timeline, mitigation, and customer impact numbers) — owner: Marcus.
- Credits/compensation proposal for Atlas — owner: Evelyn (I can provide traffic impact numbers).
- Confirm long term fix: more conservative retry-limiter defaults + edge autoscaling for Dedicated pools — owners: Jonas + Infra.

Sean — looping you because Atlas is requesting compensation and exec comms.

Jonas Weber
Director, Edge Platform
